body: Are there files in use on the mount? It can't unmount until there are no files in use.

I am not sure (is there any method to see whether the files are still in use?)

What I have done in the test is just `cd ~/mnt/test; cat ./a.txt; cd ~; exit;`, I didn't open folders or files by other apps, although I am not sure whether is any background app trying to access the mounted directory.

More information:

1. When `cmount` unmount fails and hangs (no response to ^C), the mounted folder is already empty, `ls ~/mnt/test` finishes immediately and shows nothing.

2. only `cmount` fails and hangs, `mount` can unmount successfully immediately.

3. Even if I hit ^C as soon as `cmount` started (in less than  1 second),  the `host.Unmount failed` error still occurs and the process hangs for a long time

4. The hang time is exactly 1 minute (60 seconds)

5. Sometimes although `host.Unmount failed` happens but `rclone` can exit immediately without any delay.


```
2020/11/25 22:19:07 DEBUG : rclone: Version "v1.53.3" starting with parameters ["rclone" "cmount" "-vv" "--vfs-cache-mode" "full" "remote-test:/" "/Users/user/mnt/test"]
...
...
2020/11/25 22:19:07 DEBUG : /: >Access: errc=0
^C
2020/11/25 22:19:08 INFO  : Signal received: interrupt
2020/11/25 22:19:08 DEBUG : Cache remote mount-home-storage-collection:: Services stopped
2020/11/25 22:19:08 DEBUG : Cache remote mount-home-storage-collection:: Destroy:
2020/11/25 22:19:08 DEBUG : Cache remote mount-home-storage-collection:: >Destroy:
2020/11/25 22:19:08 DEBUG : vfs cache: cleaner exiting
2020/11/25 22:19:08 DEBUG : Calling host.Unmount
2020/11/25 22:19:08 DEBUG : host.Unmount failed
2020/11/25 22:19:08 INFO  : Exiting...
```

Big Sur is the latest release macOS isn't it? (Sorry not a mac user). So do you think this is a regression to do with that rather than anything else?

When rclone is hung so when it has printed `Exiting...` can you kill the rclone process with `kill -QUIT pid-of-rclone`

This should generate a backtrace which shows exactly where rclone is stuck - can you post it here please?

Here is where rclone prints that message - note the Exit immediately after which is puzzling...

https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/979bb07c86f9680466e9421da116aaf3af94c1da/lib/atexit/atexit.go#L45-L46

Sorry I didn't mean it is a regression ( I just have only macOS 11 Big Sur ....)

Very strange, the `kill -QUIT` doesn't give any output, it seems that the `rclone` process has entered a exiting state:
```
$ ps ax | grep rclone
21683 s000  ?E+    0:00.00 (rclone)
```

I think the duration of the hang time is exactly 1 minute during my several tests.

Sometimes although `host.Unmount failed` happens but `rclone` can exit immediately without any delay.

I looked into the `fuse` repo, it seems that the `unmount` doesn't report `errno` so we can not debug with errno easily.  https://github.com/billziss-gh/cgofuse/blob/master/fuse/host_cgo.go#L588 


This problem may be not that serious but a little annoying ...

(I am using oh-my-zsh with timestamp on the prompt)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2114189/100405753-3742f380-309f-11eb-9c00-a5e84113b19d.png)

> Very strange, the `kill -QUIT` doesn't give any output, it seems that the `rclone` process has entered a exiting state:
> 
> ```
> $ ps ax | grep rclone
> 21683 s000  ?E+    0:00.00 (rclone)
> ```

That kind of implies the rclone process has exited. According to the (BSD) man page

> +       The process is in the foreground	process	group of its		       control terminal.
> E       The process is trying to	exit.

So I think the OS must be keeping it alive for some reason. This is probably because the `host.Unmount` didn't work properly. This has been discussed here https://github.com/billziss-gh/cgofuse/issues/6 in the past.

I wonder if this is caused by rclone intercepting CTRL-C and not letting libfuse handle it.

I traced the code and I discovered
- sometimes the unmount is called twice when a signal is received
- rclone and cgofuse/libfuse are racing to see who can shutdown the filesystem when a signal is received

I've attempted to fix both of these here - hopefully this will fix your problem - can you give it a go?

[v1.54.0-beta.4926.a98cb2da0.fix-4804-umount](https://beta.rclone.org/branch/fix-4804-umount/v1.54.0-beta.4926.a98cb2da0.fix-4804-umount/) on branch [fix-4804-umount](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/tree/fix-4804-umount) (uploaded in 15-30 mins)

```
2020/11/27 19:19:19 DEBUG : /: Releasedir: fh=0x0
2020/11/27 19:19:19 DEBUG : /: >Releasedir: errc=0
^C
2020/11/27 19:19:20 INFO  : Signal received: interrupt
2020/11/27 19:19:20 DEBUG : Cache remote home-storage-user-collection:: Services stopped
2020/11/27 19:19:20 DEBUG : Cache remote home-storage-user-collection:: Destroy:
2020/11/27 19:19:20 DEBUG : Not calling host.Unmount as signal received
2020/11/27 19:19:20 DEBUG : Cache remote home-storage-user-collection:: >Destroy:
2020/11/27 19:19:20 DEBUG : vfs cache: cleaner exiting
2020/11/27 19:19:20 DEBUG : Unmounted successfully
2020/11/27 19:19:20 INFO  : Exiting...
```

Result:
* No 'failed' message, but `Unmounted successfully`
* It still hangs for 1 minute exactly, the stop time is `19:20:20`

OK, thanks for testing. I think rclone is doing the right thing now.

Can you try the cgofuse example and see if you get the same problem? You'll need Go installed for this.

```
$ go get github.com/billziss-gh/cgofuse/examples/hellofs

In a new window

hello

hello, world
```

Then CTRL-C the first one

As another method: This command forces an unmount when rclone mount hangs (in Big Sur and other versions)

`diskutil unmountDisk force /Volumes/MacDrive/Users/Username/Mountname`

Insert the location of your own mount of course. I find using the full path is most effective.

Separately: I'm finding that cmount and mount do not work with Big Sur and older versions of MacFuse. However, using beta MacFuse 4.0.3 and  rclone v1.54.0-beta.4932.bcbe393af the mount is successful but then after an hour or more it randomly fails (The mount disappears. I I suspect a Fuse+Big Sur issue not an rclone issue). Using an older version of Mac OS all still works fine. Will keep playing and post separately if the problem persists.

repository.description: Perkeep (née Camlistore) is your personal storage system for life: a way of storing, syncing, sharing, modelling and backing up content.

issue.body:
Based on some code review perkeep uses bazil.org/fuse which do not support macFuse 4 because of the license issue.
Some projects such as rclone cmount they switch to github.com/billziss-gh/cgofuse.

Some useful references:
https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/3096
https://github.com/plexdrive/plexdrive/issues/390#issuecomment-737315337
https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/4804
